newsitem.title: UK: Crop forecaster sees higher 1996/97 UK wheat crop.
newsitem.headline: Crop forecaster sees higher 1996/97 UK wheat crop.

text.p: UK wheat crop could rise to a revised 15.74 million tonnes (previously 15.04 million) in 1996/97 (Oct-Sept) from 14.31 million in 1995/96, UK trade firm Allied Grain Group said on Tuesday.
The company also revised upward its forecast for the UK barley crop to 7.74 million tonnes (7.50 million) for the coming harvest, up from 6.85 million in 1995/96.
An oats crop of 600,000 tonnes completes the cereal picture to give total UK crop of just over 24 million tonnes for the coming harvest, up from its earlier estimate of 23.1 million.

Allied said the upward revision for wheat followed the latest June census area figures released by the Agriculture Ministry last Thursday as well as better-than-expected yields in the later cut crops in the north.
The ministry census results for wheat showed a significant increase over the area predicted in the Home-Grown Cereals Authority (HGCA) planting survey.
Allied had last week voiced concern over the surplus disposal problems due to the good harvest.

But in a statement on Tuesday the company said the UK had got off to a good start with lower prices allowing the UK to take a larger-than-expected share of the European Union market in the early season.

"Exports of wheat for August and September are on target to pass 750,000 tonnes but they will need to continue at or above these levels for the next nine months to soak up this record crop, and a firming of prices is therefore unlikey," it said.
On barley, Allied said the Scottish spring barley has surprised many growers in its size, and yield increases of 20 percent over last year were not uncommon.
"Intervention may now feature this season for barley due to the increased production and limited export opportunities," the company said.
